text:
maria: Quick heads-up — I'm opening a PR to compress the networking module boundaries so service accounts + k8s secret wiring live in infra/shared instead of being cross-stack in app-namespace. This should reduce the cross-module refs and make state moves deterministic.

maria: Plan is to: pin the module-level aws provider to 4.18.0, add a small migration var `migration_mode = true`, and produce a lockfile via `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64`. Will push the lockfile in the same PR.

maria: Draft snippet:
```hcl
module "net_core" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com:redwood/infra-modules.git//network?ref=compact-v2"
  providers = {
    aws = aws.network
  }
  region = var.region
}
```

kai: :eyes: quick q — are we changing provider aliases? If existing stacks use `aws` no-alias, moving to `aws.network` could cause plan diffs unless we keep compatibility.

maria: Good point. I'll keep the module provider mapping compatible by adding the provider map but not changing top-level provider names. So top-level still exposes `provider "aws" {}` and we add an aliased one only inside the module to avoid forcing consumers to update.

sam: For the k8s secret stuff: will the `kubernetes` provider remain per-cluster, or do we centralize a single provider in infra/shared? Concerned about RBAC scopes.

zhen: For EKS resources we should keep cluster-scoped providers where they belong. We can centralize the secret creation (namespaced k8s objects) into infra/shared but still pass the per-cluster `kubeconfig` into the module. That avoids access escalation.

maria: Exactly — module will accept `kubeconfig` and `k8s_provider_config` inputs. No cross-cluster creds.

kai: Also triple-check state mv commands. You'll want something like:
```bash
terraform state mv module.old_network.aws_eks_cluster.cluster module.net_core.aws_eks_cluster.cluster
terraform state mv module.old_network.kubernetes_secret.app_creds module.net_core.kubernetes_secret.app_creds
```
Plan against staging after those moves.

maria: Yep, I'll include the state-move plan steps in the PR body.

olivia: Can you run a plan in the staging workspace and post the run link? I can watch for any drift and smoke the app.

devops-bot: CI queued: `infra/plan (staging)` — https://ci.redwoodinfra.internal/runs/INFR-4212 (will post status)

devops-bot: apply pending manual approval in `infra/apply (staging)` once plan looks clean.

sam: One more — lockfile changes are fine but please add a short note in the PR describing how to regenerate (OS/platform flags) so ops can reproduce. Also CTL to revert if lockfile causes provider resolution oddities.

maria: Will do. I'll also pin `required_providers` in the module to avoid surprises and add a test job that runs `terraform init -lockfile=auto` in a matrix for linux/amd64 and macos/arm64.

zhen: Sounds safe. If staging plan is 0 (after state mv) then we can canary apply to a single region.

maria: Thanks all — I'll push the branch now and drop the PR link. @kai @sam please ping me if you want to review the state move steps specifically.

maria: PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1874 (draft, lockfile included)

kai: Reviewing now.

sam: I'll queue the staging smoke once the plan completes.

maria: Closing loop — I'll tag you both when staging apply finishes.
